belongs_to: Opening of 'Making it More or Less': 'Observe these two figures. Is there any similarity or difference between the two?' - the FIRST figure (perimeter 12 units, area 9 sq units)
description: A 3 x 3 square made of 9 unit squares: 3 rows and 3 columns, every unit square outlined in black, all 9 filled with the same light lavender (about #c5c9e5). No numbers, labels or dimensions on it. It is printed on the left, side by side with the second figure (P17-shape-2); same unit-square size in both. The text says its area is 9 sq units and its perimeter 12 units.

belongs_to: Opening of 'Making it More or Less': 'Observe these two figures...' - the SECOND figure (the text says perimeter 20 units, area 9 sq units)
description: A C-shaped (open-box) figure made of 9 unit squares in 3 rows, drawn in a 4-column by 3-row frame: top row = 4 squares (columns 1-4); middle row = ONE square only, in column 1 (the left end); bottom row = 4 squares (columns 1-4). So the three cells of the middle row in columns 2-4 are empty and form a notch open to the right. Every unit square is outlined in black and filled with a darker periwinkle blue (about #a3abd6) than figure 1. No labels or dimensions. Printed on the right of P17-shape-1, same unit-square size, same top and bottom edge height. Count: 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 squares.

belongs_to: 'Let's do something tricky now! We have a figure below having perimeter 24 units. Without calculating all over again, observe, think and find out what will be the change in the perimeter if a new square is attached as shown on the right.' - the LEFT figure on the grid (the starting figure)
description: Drawn on one sheet of grid paper that is 18 columns wide and 9 rows high (162 white unit cells, thin dark-grey lines, no numbers). Cell addresses below are (row, column), row 1 = top row, column 1 = left column. LEFT figure = a plus-like figure of 11 shaded unit squares (light blue-lavender fill, about #b0b7dc): row 3: column 5; row 4: columns 5 and 7; row 5: columns 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 (a horizontal bar of 5); row 6: columns 3 and 5; row 7: column 5. So a vertical bar of 5 squares in column 5 (rows 3-7) crosses a horizontal bar of 5 squares in row 5 (columns 3-7), with two extra single squares: one above the right end of the horizontal bar at (4,7) and one below its left end at (6,3). Count verified: 1 + 2 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 11 squares; its perimeter is 24 units (stated in the text). No labels. The sheet is shared with P17-shape-4: the left figure occupies columns 3-7, the right figure columns 12-16, columns 8-11 are empty between them.

belongs_to: Same 'tricky' question: 'what will be the change in the perimeter if a new square is attached as shown on the right' - the RIGHT figure on the grid (same figure plus the new square and its arrow); also the figure for the next page's 'Experiment placing this new square at different places... a) increases b) decreases c) stays the same'
description: Drawn on one sheet of grid paper that is 18 columns wide and 9 rows high (162 white unit cells, thin dark-grey lines, no numbers). Cell addresses below are (row, column), row 1 = top row, column 1 = left column. RIGHT figure = an exact copy of the left figure (P17-shape-3) moved 9 columns to the right: 11 shaded squares at row 3: column 14; row 4: columns 14 and 16; row 5: columns 12, 13, 14, 15, 16; row 6: columns 12 and 14; row 7: column 14. PLUS one separate new unit square (same lavender fill, outlined in black) drawn near the bottom right of the figure, slightly OFF the grid lines (not aligned to the cells): it lies roughly in column 17, spanning about rows 7-8. A short curved DASHED arrow with an open arrowhead starts at the top of the new square and points up and to the left; the arrowhead ends inside the empty grid cell (6,15) - the cell directly right of the shaded square (6,14) and directly below the shaded square (5,15). So the arrow shows the new square being attached at that cell, where it would touch two sides (the square above it and the square on its left). No numbers or labels.
unclear: The arrow tip is read as pointing at cell (6,15); the arrow is drawn between cells, so the target cell is judged from where the arrowhead sits.
The loose new square is drawn a little off the grid (about column 17, rows 7-8); its exact offset is approximate.

belongs_to: 'Below is the house plan of Charan. It is in a rectangular plot. Look at the plan. What do you notice?' ... 'Some of the measurements are given. a. Find the missing measurements. b. Find out the area of his house.'
description: A floor plan of Charan's house in a rectangular plot, on a pale pink panel (about #fce6e6); room walls are thick blue lines (about #4c82c1) and the room interiors are the same pale pink. A vertical double-headed arrow just right of the plot spans the full height of the plot; its label '30 ft' is written (rotated) in the middle of the arrow, breaking the line. No horizontal length is printed. Printed room labels, each centred in its room: (1) MASTER BEDROOM: 'Master Bedroom / (15 ft x 15 ft) / Area=225 sq ft' (top-left room). (2) TOILET: a narrow tall room right of the Master Bedroom, text rotated 90 degrees clockwise (reads top to bottom): 'Toilet / (5ft x 10 ft)' (no area printed). (3) UTILITY: a thin wide strip at the top-right corner: 'Utility / (____ ft x ____ ft) / Area = ____' (blanks), text cramped to the strip's height. (4) KITCHEN: below Utility, right of the Toilet: 'Kitchen / (15 ft x 12 ft) / Area = 180 sq ft'. (5) SMALL BEDROOM: below the Master Bedroom, same width: 'Small Bedroom / (15 ft x ____ ft) / Area = 180 sq ft'. (6) HALL: the big middle/right room, label 'Hall / Area = ____' (no dimensions line printed). (7) GARDEN: a thin strip along the bottom-left (under the Small Bedroom and part of the Hall): 'Garden / (____ ft x ____ ft) / Area = ____'. (8) PARKING: thin strip at the bottom-right: 'Parking / (____ ft x ____ ft) / Area = ____'. Layout (8 rooms): the left column holds Master Bedroom (top) over Small Bedroom; the Toilet sits at the top between the left column and the right block; at the top-right Utility is above Kitchen; the Hall fills the rest of the middle and right: it is an L-shape - a short narrow part under the Toilet (between Master Bedroom side and Kitchen) and a wide part under the Kitchen down to the bottom strip; the Garden and Parking strips run along the whole bottom edge of the plot, side by side, divided by a vertical wall that lines up with the wall between the Toilet/narrow Hall part and the Kitchen (Garden is about 4/7 of the bottom width, Parking about 3/7). Drawn to scale (measured from the picture, about 35 pixels per foot; NOT printed): plot 35 ft wide x 30 ft high; with the top-left corner as origin (x right, y down, in ft): Master Bedroom x 0-15, y 0-15; Toilet x 15-20, y 0-10; Utility x 20-35, y 0-3; Kitchen x 20-35, y 3-15; Small Bedroom x 0-15, y 15-27; Hall = x 15-20, y 10-15 plus x 15-35, y 15-27; Garden x 0-20, y 27-30; Parking x 20-35, y 27-30.
unclear: The ft values in the last sentence are measured from the drawn proportions, not printed; only the labels quoted above are printed.
The text extraction of this page wrongly puts '(15 ft x ____ ft)' under Hall; in the picture that line belongs to the Small Bedroom and the Hall has only 'Hall / Area = ____'.

belongs_to: 'Now, find out the missing dimensions and area of Sharan's home. Below is the plan:' ... 'a. Find the missing measurements. b. Find out the area of his house.' and 'Compare the areas and perimeters of Sharan's house and Charan's house.'
description: A floor plan of Sharan's house on a pale pink panel (about #fce6e6) with thick blue room walls (about #4c82c1). Seven rooms with printed labels: (1) MASTER BEDROOM (top-left): 'Master Bedroom / (12 ft x 15 ft) / Area=180 sq ft'. (2) SMALL BEDROOM (bottom-left, below Master Bedroom, same width): 'Small Bedroom / (12 ft x 10 ft) / Area = ____'. (3) TOILET (narrow tall room at the top, right of the Master Bedroom): horizontal text wrapped over 5 lines: 'Toilet / (____ ft x / ____ ft) / Area = / ____'. (4) KITCHEN (top, right of the Toilet): 'Kitchen / (18 ft x 10 ft) / Area = 180 sq ft'. (5) UTILITY (top-right corner, narrow): text rotated 90 degrees clockwise: 'Utility / (____ ft x ____ ft) / Area = 70 sq ft'. (6) ENTRANCE (right edge, below Utility, tall narrow): text rotated 90 degrees clockwise: 'Entrance / (____ ft x ____ ft) / Area = ____'. The Toilet-Kitchen wall and the Kitchen-Utility wall go from the top edge down to that horizontal wall. Drawn to scale (measured from the picture, about 33 pixels per foot; NOT printed): plot 42 ft wide x 25 ft high; origin top-left (x right, y down, ft): Master Bedroom x 0-12, y 0-15; Small Bedroom x 0-12, y 15-25; Toilet x 12-17, y 0-10; Kitchen x 17-35, y 0-10; Utility x 35-42, y 0-10; Entrance x 35-42, y 10-25; Hall x 12-35, y 10-25.

belongs_to: 'Area Maze Puzzles: In each figure, find the missing value of either the length of a side or the area of a region.' - figure a.
description: Figure 'a.' (letter printed above the top-left corner). One rectangle split by one full-height vertical line and one full-width horizontal line into 4 rectangles (2 columns x 2 rows), all outlined in black, no outside dimension arrows. The left column is narrow (about 1/3 of the width), the right column wide (about 2/3). The top row is a little shorter than the bottom row. Labels: top-left '13 sq cm'; top-right '26 sq cm'; bottom-left '15 sq cm'; bottom-right '? sq cm' with this region filled light pink (about #f8cfd0). The other three regions are white.

Figure 'b.' (letter printed above its top-left). Three rectangles in a staircase, all outlined in black, drawn to scale (about 83 px per cm): (1) a horizontal rectangle at the bottom-left labelled '10 sq cm'; (2) a tall vertical rectangle labelled '10 sq cm' (text on two lines '10 sq / cm') standing on the right part of the top edge of (1): its left edge is inset from (1)'s left edge, its right edge lines up with (1)'s right edge; (3) a square at the top right labelled '? sq cm', filled light pink (about #f8cfd0), whose left edge is (2)'s right edge and whose top is level with (2)'s top; its bottom edge ends well above the level of (1)'s top edge, leaving an empty gap below it, to the right of (2) and above (1)'s right end. Dimension arrows (double-headed, black): a horizontal arrow over the pink square labelled '3 cm' (its width); a vertical arrow at the right of (2), under the pink square, from the pink square's bottom edge down to the level of (1)'s top edge, labelled '2 cm'; a horizontal arrow above (1)'s top-left overhang (between (1)'s left edge and (2)'s left edge) labelled '3 cm'; a vertical arrow at the left of (1) spanning its full height labelled '2 cm'. Drawn proportions: (1) about 5 units wide x 2 high; (2) about 2 wide x 5 high; pink about 3 x 3 (as drawn, consistent with the arrows).

Figure 'c.' (letter printed above its top-left). Three rectangles stacked with their LEFT edges aligned, all outlined in black: TOP: a roughly square rectangle labelled '? sq cm', filled light pink (about #f8cfd0), narrower than the middle one; MIDDLE: a wider rectangle labelled '42 sq cm'; BOTTOM: the widest rectangle labelled '60 sq cm'. Dimension arrows: a long vertical double-headed arrow at the far left spanning the whole stack (top of the pink rectangle to the bottom of the 60 sq cm rectangle), labelled '15 cm'; a horizontal arrow right of the pink rectangle, from the pink rectangle's right edge to the middle rectangle's right edge, labelled '3 cm' (label below the arrow); a vertical arrow at the right of the middle rectangle spanning the middle rectangle's full height, labelled '6 cm'; a horizontal arrow along the top edge of the bottom rectangle, from the middle rectangle's right edge to the bottom rectangle's right edge, labelled '5 cm' (label above the arrow).
unclear: Not clearly to scale (the 6 cm arrow looks shorter than 6/15 of the 15 cm arrow); only the printed numbers matter.

description: Figure 'd.' (letter printed above its top-left). Two rectangles side by side sharing a vertical edge and with their bottom edges level, outlined in black: LEFT: a tall rectangle labelled '38 sq cm'; above its top edge a horizontal double-headed arrow spanning the full top width, with a light pink (about #f8cfd0) label box '? cm' above the arrow; RIGHT: a shorter, wider rectangle labelled '18 sq cm' whose top is lower than the left rectangle's top; a horizontal double-headed arrow just inside/along its top edge spanning its full width labelled '5 cm' (label above the arrow). Between the two tops, to the right of the left rectangle and above the right rectangle, a vertical double-headed arrow runs from the level of the left rectangle's top edge down to the right rectangle's top edge, labelled '4 cm' (label to its right). Drawn proportions: left about 5 wide x 7.5 high, right about 5 wide x 3.6 high.
